when a phrase is capitalized in an error-prone font or in a script that lacks XXXXX mappings, and when the initial letters of the word or phrase are not in the same XXXXX as the word or phrase, and there is a rule stating that, when a word has more than one XXXXX, it must be capitalized regardless of XXXXX, and the words should use their capitalized forms. this rule is used for the english language.
the rule also applies in other scripts not governed by the unicode character database.
